svg.title: kP, the spring: push = kP × error
svg.desc: Animated. A block sits on a floor, tied by a spring to a dashed target line. The block is pulled out to some distance from the target, held, then pulled out twice as far, held, and let go: it slides back to the target. A blue arrow on the block shows the push toward the target, and it is always proportional to the distance, the error: twice the error, twice the push, and no push on the target. Below, a straight-line graph of push against error, with a dot riding the line in step with the block, marks 1 times and 2 times. Footer: steering kP 0.01 means 1% of the battery per degree, so 10 degrees of error gives 0.1 times 12 V, 1.2 V.
svg.text: kP, the spring: push = kP × error
P is proportional: twice the error, twice the push.
Like a spring: the further from the target, the harder it pulls.
In REV units, steering kP 0.01 means 1% of the battery per degree,
so 10° of error gives 0.1 × 12 V = 1.2 V.
